decisions.statement: An account is judged from the two stamps the upkeep writes beside its page and from nothing else.
A token's remaining life is judged against a floor computed from the upkeep's own margin and period.
The ceiling a usage reading's age is judged against is computed from the upkeep's own period.
An upkeep run is legitimately late by at most two of the upkeep's periods.
A usage reading is allowed one further period of slack past a missed run.
The worst fault found is the verdict answered.
An expired token is answered ahead of a stale usage reading.
An account with neither stamp has never been reached rather than fallen behind.
A stamp sitting beside a page as anything but a timestamp reads as unread.
An account that could not be looked at reads as unread rather than as behind.
An account that reads as unread is counted out of the accounts judged.
An account that reads as unread is named among neither the stalled nor the current.
Every ruling states the count of pages and the count judged and the count current.
Every span is stated in hours to one decimal place.
An account whose beside would not read is answered on its own rather than refusing the listing.
An account held with a provider the upkeep never reaches is not judged here.
Every instant a verdict is judged against is handed in by the caller.
The two keys read here are spelled as the model-account page type declares those keys.
Nothing here reads a clock.
Nothing here fetches.
Nothing here writes.
Nothing here reads a secret or a token.
A page with nothing beside that page has never been reached rather than reading as unread.

definition: how far behind the upkeep an account has fallen
